name: FirstGroup plc
executive_summary: FirstGroup plc screens as a strong buy (15/22 models, composite 86%, 5/5 families, P/E 8.7, yield 4.0%, ROE 16.7%) on a UK bus-and-rail group that is already mid-transition: South Western Railway has transferred to the DfT Operator, Great Western’s National Rail Contract expires on 13 December 2026, West Coast Partnership is expected around the end of FY27, and the residual is First Bus plus open-access and contracted rail, including London Overground (mobilised 3 May 2026). The usable cash figure for cover is company-defined free cash flow of £73.8m in the FY26 results RNS, not the filing-aligned OCF−capex £362.6m or the suppressed screen TTM £302.8m; on that conservative basis FY26 cash dividends of £38.9m plus the completed £50.4m buyback already exceeded one year of company FCF, so the new £100m programme plus the ordinary dividend is a multi-year, balance-sheet and disposal-proceeds story. Research overlays have already cut the headline to Accumulate / adjusted buy. This pass keeps that overlay: cheapness on adjusted earnings is real, economic net debt is low, but the screen’s dividend and FCF-yield families still pass while FCF-definition flags stay false and the continuing mix is not the group those multiples describe. Twelve weeks at strong_buy with RSI 35 and the price about 2.5% below the 200-day average is persistence, not a fresh cheapness event.
investment_thesis:
The screen’s cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk-family passes describe a still-consolidated operator that includes remaining DfT TOC management-fee income. Those fees are rolling off into public ownership. What continues is a larger First Bus (FY26 revenue £1,443.6m, adjusted operating profit £102.8m) with London franchising already inside the mix, open access that is growing in journeys but margin-pressed (FY26 open-access adjusted operating profit £25.6m after Stirling mobilisation and the Lumo infrastructure charge), and an Overground concession of about £300m anticipated FY27 revenue where TfL retains revenue risk and the profit margin is not disclosed. Adjusted EPS did rise — 20.3p versus 19.4p — on a smaller weighted-average share count (553.4m versus 597.7m), and filing-adjusted net debt of £137.7m is modest once IFRS 16 rail leases and ring-fenced cash are stripped. That is an accumulate case on the earnings and leverage lines, not a value trap.

It is not a strong buy on cash. Company-defined FCF fell from £113.5m to £73.8m; H1 FY26 was a £35.6m free-cash outflow on accelerated bus electrification; and Yahoo operating cash flow / FCF also stepped down (OCF £754.2m to £615.6m, FCF £597.8m to £362.6m). The Yahoo statutory series (revenue £4,653.5m to £4,332.7m, net income £127.5m to £118.3m) looks like an earnings collapse; the FY26 RNS shows the opposite on the adjusted perimeter that management steers — adjusted revenue £1,370.0m to £1,715.7m — because statutory rail pass-through left with SWR. A value investor is therefore underwriting a policy-transition mix and an FCF definition, not a broken franchise. The embedded limit plan at £173.14 / £166.14 buys that transition at a modest discount to a 4.0% yield; that is acceptable for an accumulate book and too aggressive if the screen’s FCF-yield pass is the reason for full-size entry.
financial_review:
Reporting currency is pounds sterling throughout the FY 2026 results RNS (52 weeks to 28 March 2026, published 18 June 2026; `/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/FGP.L/20260904T164856Z/sources/filings/bodies/3bf5ff09fbc5c747.txt`). Prefer these figures over Yahoo: the FY26 income extract in `financials_annual.json` omits EPS and share count that FY25 has.

Group, same annual RNS. Adjusted revenue £1,715.7m (FY25 £1,370.0m, +25%). Statutory continuing revenue £4,751.9m (FY25 restated £5,233.9m), driven by First Rail DfT TOC pass-through of £3,327.6m (FY25 restated £4,180.7m). Group adjusted operating profit (continuing) £219.4m (FY25 £222.8m), marginally lower; excluding DfT TOCs, adjusted operating profit grew 18%. Statutory continuing operating profit £219.4m (FY25 £222.6m) — FY26 had no adjusting items, so statutory and adjusted operating profit match. Adjusted EPS (continuing) 20.3p (FY25 19.4p); total adjusted EPS 20.7p including discontinued 0.4p; basic/statutory EPS 21.4p (FY25 21.3p). Weighted-average shares 553.4m (FY25 597.7m); shares in issue 542.6m excluding treasury and EBT.

First Bus versus First Rail versus open access versus contracted, same RNS. First Bus adjusted/statutory revenue £1,443.6m (FY25 £1,081.5m): Regional Bus £891.3m, Business & Coach £230.1m, Franchising £322.2m including about £310m First Bus London. First Bus adjusted operating profit £102.8m (+7% versus £96.0m). First Rail adjusted revenue £272.4m (FY25 £288.8m), split DfT TOCs & Rail Services £130.6m and open access/rail contracts £141.8m. First Rail adjusted operating profit £129.9m (FY25 £148.8m), of which open-access adjusted operating profit £25.6m (FY25 £34.1m). Open-access revenue £109.3m on 3.1m journeys (+4%). London Overground was awarded in December 2025 and mobilised on 3 May 2026: eight-year term plus a two-year TfL option, about £300m anticipated revenue in FY27 and about £3bn over the contract life, with TfL retaining revenue risk. That is contracted operator economics, not a replacement TOC fee stream; the RNS does not disclose the concession margin.

Conflict check on Yahoo versus filing earnings. Yahoo FY26 total revenue £4,332.7m and net income £118.3m (`financials_annual.json`) sit below filing statutory continuing revenue £4,751.9m. Yahoo net income is consistent with filing statutory EPS 21.4p on the 553.4m weighted-average count (about £118.4m) and is the continuing-plus-discontinued statutory result, not a second earnings series. Use the RNS for revenue and mix; use Yahoo NI only as a statutory cross-check. The Business Standard “FGP standalone NI −11%” item is Indian standalone reporting and is not FirstGroup plc.

Cash and the three FCF bases. FY26 results RNS: cash generated by operations £681.5m (FY25 £828.2m); cash capex £(253.0)m (FY25 £(156.4)m); First Bus net capex £188.2m, with highlights citing about £190m accelerated electrification and about £35m growth investment/acquisitions. Company-defined free cash flow is £73.8m (FY25 £113.5m), described as before acquisitions and returns; the cash-flow table adds back dividends £38.9m and the buyback £50.4m to reach that £73.8m / £113.5m pair. Group adjusted cash flow was £(124.0)m (FY25 £(18.8)m) after capex, acquisitions, leases and returns — a wider outflow than company FCF, not a second FCF definition that can be added through to £73.8m.

Conflict check on FCF. `screening_snapshot.json` records filing £362.6m, screen TTM £302.8m and company-adjusted £73.8m, with `fcf_basis_overlay` true but `fcf_definition_divergence` and `fcf_divergence_flagged` both false. The £362.6m is Yahoo operating cash flow £615.6m minus capex £253.0m in `financials_annual.json` / `fcf_bridge.json`; it is not printed as “FCF” in the FY26 RNS and overstates equity cash versus management’s definition. Screen TTM £302.8m sits on a suppressed TTM (`ttm_cashflow_suppressed`, reason `quarterly_cashflow_empty`) and cannot be rebuilt: Yahoo `quarterly_income` and `quarterly_cashflow` are empty. Gap-inventory cited `fcf_bridge.json` policy FCF of £113.5m for FY2026; spot-check of the FY26 RNS shows £73.8m for FY26 and £113.5m for FY25. The bridge file is period-locked to the wrong year (it labels £73.8m an “alternate IR slide”). Prefer the RNS. Cover versus cash dividends paid £38.9m is about 1.9× on company FCF and about 9× on the Yahoo OCF−capex figure; the latter is not a usable equity-cover test. FY26 cash returns of £38.9m dividends plus £50.4m buybacks (£89m) already exceeded company FCF; adjusted net debt rose from £86.9m to £137.7m as electrification capex and returns were funded. The announced £100m buyback plus the ~£27m final dividend cannot be funded from a single year of £73.8m company FCF. Management’s three-year free-cash guide of about £400m (raised to about £435m after Mistral) is the funding story, not FY26 run-rate.

H1 FY26 (26 weeks to 27 September 2025; Half-yearly Report 18 November 2025, `/workspace/docs/data/research_director_worker/FGP.L/20260904T164856Z/sources/filings/bodies/c1db8cdf5ad2bd84.txt`). Group adjusted revenue £833.6m (H1 2025 £639.6m, +30%); adjusted operating profit £103.6m (£100.8m); margin 12.4% versus 15.8%; adjusted EPS 9.9p versus 8.5p on weighted-average shares 559.7m versus 608.5m. First Bus revenue £702.9m (+37%); adjusted operating profit £42.7m (+4%); margin 6.1% versus 8.0%. Underlying bus passenger volumes −4% excluding London and post-H1 2025 acquisitions (concessionary +4%, commercial −7%), attributed to the £3 fare cap, weaker consumer confidence and modal shift; reported passenger volumes 196m versus 204m excluding London. First Rail adjusted revenue £130.9m; adjusted operating profit £66.6m, of which DfT TOC £39.7m and open access plus Rail Services £26.9m. Free cash outflow £35.6m (H1 2025 +£2.6m); adjusted cash outflow £212.2m; cash capex £136.4m; First Bus net capex £110.6m. Adjusted net debt £207.6m at 27 September 2025 (FY25 £86.9m). Interim dividend 2.2p (about £12.0m). Management called this a “period of transition”; the ~10% share-price drop on results day is title-only in the news manifest and matches this print’s volume, cash-outflow and debt colour rather than an earnings miss. H1 bus-volume weakness is both transitory (fare-cap step-up, confidence) and structural (franchising already £155.4m in H1, including First Bus London £150.2m). FY26 full-year Bus profit still rose 7%, so the volume dip did not reverse filing-adjusted earnings.

Leverage, cash and leases, FY26 RNS. Unrestricted cash £169.6m; ring-fenced cash £262.4m (First Rail £260.8m, other £1.6m). Reported net debt £725.3m (FY25 £985.6m). Adjusted net debt £137.7m (FY25 £86.9m), excluding IFRS 16 leases and ring-fenced cash. Pre-IFRS 16 bonds/bank/other debt net of cash was a £124.7m net cash position. IFRS 16 lease liabilities £850.0m (rail £702.3m, non-rail £147.7m); DfT TOC leases on balance sheet £649.2m (FY25 £1,020.4m). Yahoo FY26 total debt £1,005m, capital-lease obligations £850m, working capital −£388m, D/E 161% versus screen D/E 19% on the £137.7m figure (`screening_snapshot.json`, `financials_annual.json`). `leverage_override` and `dual_leverage_display` stayed false: the screen already uses filing-adjusted D/E and did not surface the Yahoo gross-up. Economic leverage is low on adjusted net debt if rail IFRS 16 and ring-fenced cash are accepted as non-recourse to the residual group; non-rail leases of £147.7m and negative working capital remain. Ring-fenced cash is not available for dividends or buybacks.

Dividend, buybacks and share count. FY26 total dividend 7.2p (final proposed 5.0p; FY25 6.5p); policy about 3× cover of adjusted earnings, tightening toward 2.5× (about 2.8× on 20.3p / 7.2p). Cash dividends paid £39m (external £38.9m). A £50m buyback completed in FY26; a further £100m programme was announced with the results, expected within 12 months. Launch RNS `152c483b0284d525.txt` (gap-inventory read): four tranches of up to £25m, deadline 17 June 2027, cap 84,323,374 shares (14.99% issued), treasury then cancellation. Tranche 1 completed 24 July 2026: 13,553,662 shares for £24,806,895 (`478824dce96b4609.txt`). Treasury shares 27,778,020 at 28 August 2026 (`cfadd349de7818b5.txt`). Cumulative spend versus the £100m cap is not aggregated in one RNS — residual capacity is unresolved. Yahoo issued shares fell 750.7m to 570.7m; ordinary shares about 542.6m after treasury cancellation. Screen P/E 8.7, yield 4.0% and ROE 16.7% are post-buyback in spirit: ROE of 16.7% matches Yahoo statutory NI £118.3m on book equity of about £710m; Yahoo FY26 omits EPS and share count, so the exact P/E denominator is not in that file. Use filing WAS 553.4m / 542.6m in issue, not a reconstructed Yahoo EPS.

Corporate actions the five-task cap omitted (gap-inventory bodies). London Overground preferred-operator RNS `aefbcf7637993f73.txt`: start 3 May 2026, eight years plus up to two years, about £3bn over eight years, TfL revenue risk, profit margin on concession payments with performance-fee upside, £30m performance bond and £80m parent-company guarantee — annual profit not disclosed. Mistral Data sale agreed 29 July 2026 (`1c5ad278ca15df7c.txt`): £48m cash enterprise value; FY26 revenue about £13m and operating profit about £4m; FY27 First Rail adjusted operating profit about −£4m and group adjusted EPS about −0.6p on the 20.3p FY26 base; profit on disposal about £46m as an adjusting item; three-year free-cash guide raised to about £435m. Completion 23 August 2026 (`f8ef13aa344cabd9.txt`): £48m cash received, subject to customary adjustments. Sizewell C (`d4e60364bbdac9ab.txt`, 7 July 2026): up to five-year worker transport from July 2026, about 150 zero-emission buses supplied by Sizewell C Ltd, about 400 jobs; contract revenue/value not stated. Tootbus acquisition December 2025 (`5e08fec9f5b9088c.txt`): about £17m cash, FY2023 revenue £15.9m and operating loss £(0.6)m, about £30m annual revenue targeted by FY2029. Pre-close trading update 26 March 2026 (`4c56aaf324fdfd91.txt`): both divisions in line; modest FY26 adjusted EPS growth; year-end adjusted net debt then guided £135–145m (outturn £137.7m); fuel hedged about 88% FY27 / 53% FY28. AGM statement 30 July 2026 (`4028c725377752a6.txt`): FY-to-date trading in line with the 18 June results and the 29 July Mistral announcement; H1 FY27 results scheduled 17 November 2026 — latest formal Board trading comment. There is no post-FY26 trading update in the filings index. The 1 July AFR body `d45784fca483323c.txt` is an NSM submission notice, not the full annual-report tables.

FY27 outlook, FY26 RNS: maintain adjusted EPS from a higher-quality base; First Bus revenue just over £1.5bn with further adjusted operating-profit progress and about £140m decarbonisation capex; open-access revenue about £130–150m with margin progressing to the mid-teens; Overground about £300m; lower DfT TOC adjusted revenue; about £400m free cash over the next three years (about £90m cash inflow over three years from April 2026 as GWR/WCP transition). Post-Mistral, that cash guide is about £435m and FY27 EPS starts about 0.6p lower before any offset.

Gaps that block a residual-group score: Overground concession margin and payment schedule not disclosed; Sizewell C contract value not stated; £100m buyback residual not published as a single figure; Yahoo quarterly income and cash flow unavailable, so intra-year FCF cannot be rebuilt; alternate_news is a dead step (126 RSS titles only); FY26 results body truncated mid–going-concern section; pension notes and full statutory reconciliations (notes 3–5, 20, 22–23) are not in the assigned extract; `failed_models` is empty despite 7/22 non-passes, so the seven misses cannot be named.
risks_and_flags:
The live risk is policy transition and cash definition, not a generic industrial cycle — and the screen’s `cyclical_exposure_detected` is false. After GWR (13 December 2026) and WCP (around end-FY27) the listed equity is a bus operator plus open-access and contracted rail. Screen P/E 8.7 and the 4.0% yield still include remaining DfT TOC fees. Overground replaces some of that revenue at undisclosed margin and with TfL keeping fare risk; Mistral removes about £4m of FY27 rail profit. If bus franchising reprices the regional book, or open-access yields stay pressured (Lumo infrastructure charge, Stirling mobilisation, ORR applications still under review), the “higher-quality” EPS the Board wants to maintain is an assertion, not a residual P&L.

Bus volumes are not only a headline. H1 underlying passengers −4% and commercial −7% sat underneath a 37% Bus revenue rise that was mix and London/acquisition-driven; H1 Bus margin compressed from 8.0% to 6.1%. That can prove transitory if the fare-cap and confidence effects fade, or structural if municipal franchising spreads. The assigned FY26 extract does not give a full-year passenger KPI; do not infer a recovery that the annual worker did not print.

Cash returns depend on the optimistic FCF identity if sized off the screen. Company FCF of £73.8m covers the ordinary dividend about 1.9× and does not cover dividend plus the completed FY26 buyback, let alone the new £100m programme. Filing/Yahoo FCF of £362.6m would cover everything easily and is the figure the FCF-yield family is most likely using while `fcf_definition_divergence` stays false. Cheapness may already price a cash-return story that needs the three-year £400–435m guide, Mistral’s £48m, and remaining TOC cash inflows of about £90m (FY26 RNS) / about £125m from October 2025 (H1 RNS — the two cash-inflow guides are not reconciled in the assigned extracts). Working capital of −£388m and current-ratio stress on the Yahoo balance sheet are why Graham-defensive style models can fail even when adjusted net debt is £137.7m; those seven non-passes are unnamed because `failed_models` is [].

Leverage presentation is a second accounting overlay that did not fire. Yahoo D/E 161% versus screen 19% is IFRS 16 plus ring-fenced cash, not a hidden covenant breach in the extracts. Dual leverage should be displayed; it is not. Ring-fenced £262.4m cannot fund the buyback. Going-concern wording is truncated in the FY26 body — treat the tail as unverified. Pension risk is real for a UK transport name (shared-cost rail sections, escrow) but was not re-extracted in this worker set; leave the stock unquantified rather than reuse an older memo’s escrow figure.

Watch: H1 FY27 results on 17 November 2026; GWR handover 13 December 2026; WCP timing; Overground run-rate versus the £300m FY27 guide; remaining £100m buyback versus tranche-1 £24.8m; bus-franchising awards; any post-AGM trading comment (none since 30 July 2026). Conviction of 63% (`conviction_score` 0.628; the summary string’s 87% is a conflict inside `screening_snapshot.json`) and `stability_label` persistent are not substitutes for those monitors.

news_highlights:
`news_manifest.json` holds 126 headlines as of 4 September 2026. Coverage is RSS-heavy: Google News items are titles only — do not treat them as article-body facts. Alternate_news is unavailable. Substantive clusters match the filings.

FY26 results and the £100m buyback (18–19 June 2026): titles report revenue growth, electric-fleet expansion and a new buyback to cut share capital; a yfinance summary adds the 25% revenue increase (`#412f8f65`, `#1553b2bc`). Soft-earnings follow-ups (Simply Wall St, Kalkine, 25 June) are headline-only.

H1 2026 (18 November 2025): titles say results beat forecasts while shares fell about 10% on a “period of transition”; others cite UK bus-volume decline, cash outflow and rising debt (`#cfd060a38f6fba70`, `#d53fad78e1897f5e`). Numeric EPS, FCF and volume figures in those titles are absent — use the H1 RNS.

London Overground (December 2025): Reuters titles a $4bn contract; Proactive titles £3bn (`#797c64b30b6181da`, `#5778fb76b1ae652c`). The award RNS is about £3bn over eight years; the dollar headline is a currency conversion, not a second contract.

Mistral Data: BusinessCloud (29 July 2026) has Tracsis buying a FirstGroup arm for £48m; 24 August titles report completion, a near-7% early fall and recovery (`#fc0efea5888d7773`, `#c064eb2045550e40`). Net proceeds after adjustments are not in the titles; the completion RNS confirms £48m cash received.

Open-access / mix (September 2026): Kalkine question-headlines only — no quantitative mix data. A 12 May 2026 Proactive title says a broker sees growth despite rail nationalisation (`#6618b336bd905560`). No Sizewell C headlines are in the manifest; that award lives only in the 7 July RNS.

AGM and capital actions (July–September 2026): shareholders backed the board, dividend and capital actions (30 July); SAYE grants and option exercises; routine holdings notices. The £100m buyback prints as repeated Transaction-in-Own-Shares / TVR syndication — titled tranches include nearly 3m shares over five days (20 July), 2.77m at 179.85p (27 July), 772,452 (10–13 August) and 1.65m to treasury (24–25 August). Those titles do not sum to a residual versus £100m.

Discarded: DirectorsTalk syndicated 30–55% upside SEO; same-day buyback/TVR reprints; Business Standard “FGP standalone net profit declines 11.11%” (5 August 2026, `#8ba7396232175a4a`) — India FGP ticker collision. Institutional ownership of 77% (January 2026 yfinance) is title-only.
research_rationale: Filings confirm rising adjusted EPS and low economic net debt on a Bus-plus-contracted residual, but company-defined FCF of £73.8m does not fund the £100m buyback plus dividends in one year and the screen’s 8.7× / 4% yield still includes DfT TOC fees that expire before Overground margins are known.

open_questions: Which free-cash figure is usable for cover and for the FCF Yield / dividend-family passes: filing-aligned £362.6m, screen TTM £302.8m, or company-adjusted £73.8m — and can FY26 cash dividends paid (£38.9m Yahoo) plus buybacks (£50.4m Yahoo) plus the 18 June 2026 £100m programme be funded on the conservative basis?

After UK rail nationalisation and franchise roll-off, what is the continuing earnings mix (First Bus vs remaining First Rail vs open-access vs the London Overground preferred-operator award) and does the screen’s P/E 8.7 / 4.0% yield still describe that residual group?

Is First Bus passenger-volume weakness (H1 2026 share-price drop on “period of transition” headlines) structural municipal/franchising risk or a transitory volume dip, and did FY26 filing-adjusted earnings actually improve versus Yahoo’s FY26 revenue £4,332.7m / NI £118.3m / FCF £362.6m step-down from FY25 £4,653.5m / £127.5m / £597.8m?

Is economic leverage actually low at £137.7m adjusted net debt (screen D/E 19%) once IFRS-16 leases (Yahoo FY26 capital-lease obligations £850m, total debt £1,005m, Yahoo D/E 161%), restricted cash (£262.4m), and working capital (−£388m) are restored — and why did leverage_override / dual_leverage_display stay false?

Do the London Overground (~£3bn preferred operator, Dec 2025), December 2025 acquisition, Sizewell C transport award, and £48m Mistral Data disposal (completed 24 Aug 2026) raise or dilute returns versus the rail earnings they replace, and is cheapness already pricing a cash-return story that depends on the optimistic FCF definition?

With RSI 35, price ~2.5% below the 200-day MA, 12 weeks at strong_buy, and research already at Accumulate / medium risk (adjusted_signal buy), is the £173.14 / £166.14 limit plan buying policy-transition and FCF-definition risk too aggressively?

Yahoo FY26 income omits EPS and share count while issued shares fall 750.7m → 570.7m and ordinary shares are ~542.6m after treasury cancellation — are P/E, yield, and ROE on the post-buyback denominator, and is the Business Standard “FGP standalone NI −11%” item a different company (India FGP) rather than FirstGroup?

meta_reflection.observation: Filings-first order is adequate for a UK transport name whose live numbers sit in RNS bodies (70 local bodies; 10 annual + 7 interim + 1 trading_update in the index). It is not adequate when the FY 2026 results RNS (3bf5ff09fbc5c747, 18 Jun 2026) is catalogued period=other/priority=0, while Google News “Across the Markets”, a December 2025 Acquisition, and IR decks occupy annual/interim slots. yahoo_quarterly_cashflow is on the ladder but empty (TTM cashflow suppressed); alternate_news is a dead step while news_manifest has 126 RSS-heavy items. Trading updates are first-class in the index summary but outside the annual/interim assignment rule; the only TU is the 26 Mar 2026 pre-close, now stale versus FY26 results and the 30 Jul AGM statement.

Four worker types plus a five-task cap force annual + interim + news + screen + gap and leave no slot for London Overground, Mistral disposal/completion, the £100m buyback launch, Sizewell C, the March pre-close TU, or the July AGM statement. No task type exists to reconcile filing / TTM / company-adjusted FCF or lease vs adjusted net debt. Naive first/last-of-period selection would assign CH accounts, an IR FY25 deck tagged interim, or an Acquisition tagged annual. summarize_filing_body cannot carry period=annual|interim|trading_update|corporate_action, so directors must smuggle the FY26 results body in as “annual” despite the catalog tag.

The screen still emits strong_buy (15/22, 5/5 families including dividend and FCF Yield) while fcf_basis_overlay is true but fcf_definition_divergence and fcf_divergence_flagged stay false on a £362.6m / £302.8m / £73.8m split. Leverage overlays did not fire despite Yahoo D/E 161% vs filing-adjusted £137.7m. cyclical_exposure_detected=false on a policy-exposed bus/rail operator; interim_quality_overlay=false despite empty Yahoo quarterlies; cash_conversion_overlay=false despite OCF 754→616 and FCF 598→363. failed_models is [] despite only 15/22 passes. Research overlays already cut to Accumulate / buy, so the director–worker memo is being asked to re-verify a signal the overlay has already downgraded without changing the headline strong_buy.

A 12-week persistent strong_buy with rail nationalisation, an Overground award not yet earning, an in-flight £100m buyback, and no post-FY26 trading update has no watch schema (next TU / H1 2027, DfT franchise handback dates, Overground start, buyback completion, bus-franchising decisions). conviction_score=0.63 and stability_label=persistent are not substitutes for those monitors.

A generic FINANCIAL REVIEW / RISKS split will blend declining franchise rail with new contracted/open-access work and will not force BUS vs RAIL vs OPEN ACCESS, franchise vs contracted margin, or FCF-definition / lease-adjusted leverage sections. Without an explicit CORPORATE ACTIONS slot, workers can treat the £100m buyback, Mistral £48m sale, and Overground award as news colour rather than perimeter/capital-return facts. No required slot for ticker-collision hygiene (India FGP) or for restricted-cash vs unrestricted cash in net-debt bridges.
